records.question: The settlement: where does the cash finally settle, and in what kind of money?
records.answer: In most of what the library holds, the cash still settles in money that already existed. Swift's ledger coordinates commitments among 17 listed banks, 8 of which have a completed pairing located; final settlement happens afterwards through existing payment systems. Of the 12 market systems, 1 settles in central-bank money by the master's own description (Sterling Fnality Payment System), 4 move banks' own tokenized deposits, and for 7 the master does not say. Who finances the interval before settlement: banks validated funding and managed the interval before external settlement. Customer availability can precede bank cash receipt.

records.question: Failure and remedy: when it breaks, who can freeze, who pays, who decides?
records.answer: For 18 of the 36 crypto dollars the library tracks, the issuer can freeze or block coins; for 15 the terms read do not say. When a firm collapsed, customers were being paid back at least partly in 3 of the 10 cases on the International Crypto Map, and courts decided whether customer crypto was the customer's property or the estate's. The 7 programmable-payment failures were corrected by forks, freezes or restitution, not one rule. 37 of 41 U.S. jurisdictions in the register have enacted UCC Article 12, the law on who owns a controllable electronic record.

records.question: The world: how do the other jurisdictions do it?
records.answer: The International Crypto Map reads 22 jurisdictions on 13 dimensions each, from who has authority to who bears a loss; 191 of the 286 cells are researched, 85 partial and 10 still open. 7 of its 14 issuer records are live under a local license, 15 cross-border routes were reviewed and none is yet a recurring end-to-end corridor in the record, and most systems still finish in an existing bank or central-bank record.

records.question: The watch: what is dated, overdue, or still unknown?
records.answer: The crypto library holds 396 dated items and 308 undated clocks and open questions. 2 are past due with no record: Singapore: Stablecoin legislative consultation closes (2026-10-16); Did Treasury submit Scott Bessent's written answers from the September 15 HFSC hearing… (2026-10-20). 14 dates fall in the next 30 days: What first authoritative objects move either ARK's Exchange Class or Tokenized Class from… (2026-10-23); What does the Supreme Court do with Custodia Bank's certiorari petition in No. 26-62, and… (2026-10-28); Australia: RITS consultation closes (2026-10-30).
